title: Rumour: LEGO Jurassic World Velociraptor fossil set tipped for 2027
summary: A set number for a rumoured LEGO Jurassic World Velociraptor fossil display piece has surfaced online, suggesting the dinosaur skeleton series could continue into 2027.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to a report from Brick Fanatics, citing Unibricks, a set numbered 77987 and titled 'Dinosaur Fossils: Velociraptors' is rumoured to launch in May 2027. This would follow on from the confirmed 2025 set 76968 Dinosaur Fossils: Tyrannosaurus rex and the 2026 set 77985 Dinosaur Fossils: Triceratops.

No price or piece count has been mentioned for the rumoured Velociraptor set, so it's unclear what scale it might be built to. For comparison, the T. rex fossil set is the largest and priciest of the pair so far, with 3,145 pieces at £219.99, while the Triceratops is smaller and cheaper at 1,154 pieces for £89.99.

The plural 'Velociraptors' in the rumoured name has led to speculation that the set could feature more than one raptor skeleton in the box, though this is purely speculation at this stage and not confirmed.

## Why it matters
If accurate, this would mark a third entry in LEGO's growing Jurassic World fossil display series, a popular option for collectors and display builders who enjoy skeleton-style sets alongside traditional playsets. The scale and pricing will matter a lot to fans wanting a cohesive fossil collection on their shelves.

## What to watch next
This is currently only a rumour based on a set number and title, with no official LEGO confirmation, pricing or piece count. Fans should treat the release date, scale and contents as unconfirmed until more details or official images emerge.

title: LEGO Ideas launches Paradisa-themed building challenge
summary: LEGO Ideas has opened a new fan challenge celebrating the retro Paradisa theme, with a summer-and-flowers prize bundle worth over £700 up for grabs.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Ideas has confirmed a new official contest inviting fans to build models inspired by the classic 1990s Paradisa theme. It follows renewed interest in Paradisa sparked by recent releases including 21358 Minifigure Vending Machine and 60506 Classic Beach Streetcar.

Entries must avoid referencing any intellectual property, including LEGO Group-owned themes, but Paradisa itself is exempt, meaning minifigures based on the theme are allowed.

Five grand prize winners will each receive a bundle of sets worth £714.94, including 42691 Garden Restaurant, 21358 Minifigure Vending Machine, 11503 Flower Wall, 21359 Italian Riviera, 11505 Woodland Mushrooms and 21365 Love Birds.

The submission deadline is 9 September, though organisers suggest leaving a few extra days in case resubmission is needed.

## Why it matters
Paradisa has had a quiet resurgence lately, and an official LEGO Ideas challenge gives fans a fun, low-pressure way to engage with the theme's summery, floral aesthetic while flexing their building creativity. It's also a nice showcase for how minifigure parts from recent sets can be repurposed for retro-style builds.

## What to watch next
It'll be interesting to see whether this renewed Paradisa attention leads to further official sets or reissues down the line, though that's currently just fan speculation rather than confirmed plans.

title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer LEGO Ideas project hits 10,000 votes
summary: A Sunnydale High library build based on Buffy the Vampire Slayer has reached the 10,000-vote milestone on LEGO Ideas, giving it a shot at becoming an official set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A LEGO Ideas project recreating the library from Buffy the Vampire Slayer has reached the 10,000 supporter threshold, according to Brick Fanatics. It's the 53rd project to hit this milestone in the current review round.

Designed by fan creator Bricktoria60839, this is her third attempt at recreating the iconic Sunnydale High location, having previously entered the LEGO Ideas '90s Throwback' challenge that eventually produced the officially released 21369 The X-Files set.

The build recreates the library's dark wood interior and central research table, with details fans of the show will recognise, including LEGO Harry Potter wand pieces reused as vampire stakes. It comes with minifigures of Buffy, Giles, Willow, Angel, Xander and Spike, with Angel and Spike featuring double-sided printed heads to show their vampire faces.

Reaching 10,000 votes means LEGO Group will now consider the project during its review process, but it is **not yet confirmed** as an official set. The current review round closes on 7 September, leaving a short window for other projects to qualify.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas has increasingly turned nostalgic 1990s TV shows into official sets, so another contender in this space shows publisher appetite for the genre. For collectors and pop-culture brick fans, it's a build worth watching, though selection is far from guaranteed.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO Marvel mini modulars set to move beyond Spider-Man with Avengers Tower

Of the five newly announced Doomsday sets, two others slot into existing LEGO Marvel ranges rather than the modular street: 76345 Doctor Doom Bust joins the bust collection, and 76348 Epic Battle: Avengers: Doomsday is part of the smaller Epic Battle line.

## Why it matters
For UK collectors and display builders, this is a notable shift for a growing modular-style theme. Widening the street beyond Spider-Man opens the door to more varied Marvel buildings, which could make the collection more appealing to a broader range of fans and easier to display alongside other modular-style builds.

## What to watch next
It's worth watching for further details on 76352's release date, price and piece count, plus whether LEGO continues building out this street with more non-Spider-Man locations in future waves.

title: Mattel Brick Shop reveals two Masters of the Universe display sets
summary: Mattel's LEGO-rival construction brand is branching into Masters of the Universe with a Skeletor bust and a Havoc Staff display piece, both aimed at adult collectors.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Mattel has confirmed two new additions to its Brick Shop construction line, both tied to Masters of the Universe rather than the Hot Wheels-focused sets the brand has mostly stuck to so far.

The first is a 503-piece Skeletor Bust, priced at £43.99 in the UK, featuring three swappable face plates, a light brick and articulated points for posing. The second is a bigger 1,098-piece Havoc Staff, recreating Skeletor's signature weapon complete with a light-up ram's head and the option to display it on a stand or mount it on a wall - that one costs £59.99.

Both sets carry a 17+ age rating and are listed as 'coming soon' at UK retailers, with no firm release date yet.

Alongside these, Mattel has also confirmed a Halo UNSC M12 Warthog set (935 pieces, £69.99), landing 30 September and also aimed at adult collectors.

According to Mattel's Head of Building Sets, more new and familiar franchises are planned for the Brick Shop range through 2026.

## Why it matters
This marks a genuine shift for Mattel Brick Shop, moving away from vehicle-focused sets and metal-element gimmicks towards the kind of licensed display and bust-style builds LEGO fans will recognise from its own pop-culture ranges. For collectors interested in compatible brick brands, it's a sign Mattel is getting more ambitious - and Masters of the Universe's movie-driven popularity makes the timing sensible.

## What to watch next
